$comment: Vectors pinning the ORDER of the warnings NormalizeSAFSupplement emits for undeclared `extensions` siblings. Shared by Go and TypeScript so the two cannot drift. Each case writes its siblings in an insertion order that differs from the sorted one: Go reads them into a map and so cannot see source order, which is why the rule is code-point order of the key in both languages. Each case's `extensions` is spliced into a minimal valid results document beside a legacy top-level `passthrough`, which is what triggers the relocation.

vectors.why: three siblings, one clashing with a key already in passthrough, are reported in key order
warnings: extensions.alpha was moved into extensions.passthrough.alpha; `extensions` accepts only its defined members
extensions.mid was dropped: `extensions` is closed and extensions.passthrough.mid already holds a value
extensions.zeta was moved into extensions.passthrough.zeta; `extensions` accepts only its defined members

vectors.why: a non-object passthrough leaves every sibling in place, and reports them in key order
warnings: extensions.alpha could not be relocated because extensions.passthrough is not an object; `extensions` is closed, so this document will not validate
extensions.mid could not be relocated because extensions.passthrough is not an object; `extensions` is closed, so this document will not validate
extensions.zeta could not be relocated because extensions.passthrough is not an object; `extensions` is closed, so this document will not validate

vectors.why: key order is by code point, not UTF-16 unit: U+E000 sorts before U+10000 although its UTF-16 unit is higher, and a prefix sorts first
warnings: extensions.a was moved into extensions.passthrough.a; `extensions` accepts only its defined members
extensions.ab was moved into extensions.passthrough.ab; `extensions` accepts only its defined members
extensions. was moved into extensions.passthrough.; `extensions` accepts only its defined members
extensions.𐀀 was moved into extensions.passthrough.𐀀; `extensions` accepts only its defined members
